positioning.text: Advocate Health describes itself as the third-largest nonprofit, integrated health system in the United States, with a footprint across eight states under the Advocate Health Care, Atrium Health and Aurora Health Care brands, and says it is redefining how, when and where care is delivered.
positioning.quote: Advocate Health is redefining how, when and where care is delivered to help people live well.

facts.text: When the Advocate Aurora Health and Atrium Health combination closed on 2022-12-02, the release said the existing brands would continue to be used locally: Advocate Health Care in Illinois, Atrium Health in the Carolinas, Georgia and Alabama, and Aurora Health Care in Wisconsin.

facts.text: Advocate Health's published brand guidelines are labelled interim, keep the three care delivery brands in use with the linkage line "Now part of Advocate Health", and state that the Advocate Aurora Health logo has been discontinued.

facts.text: Advocate Health announced Kevan Mabbutt, previously at Intermountain Health, as chief marketing, communications and consumer experience officer on 2023-09-27, and Nicole Phillips, previously chief marketing officer for CVS Caremark, as chief marketing, brand and consumer officer on 2025-12-19.

facts.text: Consumer health content is published on two separate hubs: health enews, which calls itself the Midwest's go-to source for health news and links to advocatehealth.org, and Daily Dose on atriumhealth.org.

facts.text: Patient apps differ by region: LiveWell is the app and website for Advocate Health Care and Aurora Health Care patients, while Atrium Health directs patients to the MyAtriumHealth app.

facts.text: The advocatehealth.org enterprise site links to three social accounts (Facebook, LinkedIn and YouTube), while Atrium Health's Connect With Us page lists its own Facebook, Twitter, Instagram, YouTube and LinkedIn accounts plus separate accounts for Levine Children's and Levine Cancer Institute.

Becker's reported on 2026-10-15 that Atrium Health has been the Carolina Panthers' official healthcare provider since 1995 with its logo on practice uniforms, that the Panthers announced naming rights for the Atrium Health Training Facility in April 2026, and that Advocate Health Care became the Chicago Bears' official healthcare partner in 2017.

strengths.text: Keeping established regional brands while adding an enterprise linkage line lets the system hold local name recognition as it builds the Advocate Health name.
One message line, "redefining care", is repeated across the annual review, the careers site and the purpose statement.
Long-running NFL team relationships in Charlotte and Chicago give the regional brands recurring visibility.
AI deployments are announced with concrete numbers and CEO-level commentary, which supports an innovation story alongside the community benefit story.

gaps.text: The published brand guidelines are still labelled interim.
Patients use different apps depending on region (LiveWell in the Midwest brands, MyAtriumHealth for Atrium Health), so there is no single app to market system-wide.
The enterprise site links to three social accounts only; consumer accounts such as Instagram sit with the regional brands.

opportunitiesForUpmc.text: A peer whose patient apps and content hubs are split by region is a useful comparison point for how UPMC presents its own portal and health content across markets.
Advocate Health attaches numbers to its AI announcements; UPMC can check that its own AI messaging carries comparable specifics.
A single repeated line across recruitment, annual reporting and purpose is a consistency benchmark for UPMC's own message architecture.

The brand guidelines are labelled interim and a new marketing chief was announced in December 2025, so UPMC should re-check this peer's brand architecture periodically instead of treating this snapshot as settled.
